answer: Keyed storage audit: each identity must hold its own 4 GB dataset derived from hash(pubkey), cut into 64 terraces of 64 MB. Every epoch the verifier issues a quartz challenge: 8 random terrace offsets, and the identity returns those 4 KB blocks within 300 ms. Only local disk meets that; refetching from cold tundra storage or regenerating blocks misses the deadline. Each fake therefore needs 4 GB of dedicated fast disk, so 500 fakes need 2 TB, paid every epoch even if never caught, and one shared copy fails because blocks are per-key.
